links.outcome: Readability (SMOG) of LLM answers to early gastric cancer patient questions and patient-rated comprehensibility
links.effect: SMOG scores were high: DeepSeek-V3.2 14.1±1.6, ChatGPT-4o 16.4±2.3, Gemini-2.5 15.8±2.0, Grok-3 15.8±1.1. Patient comprehensibility was 79.0 for DeepSeek-V3.2 vs 88.0 for ChatGPT-4o (P<0.05).
links.quote: In terms of readability assessment, the simple measure of gobbledygook (SMOG) score for DeepSeek-V3.2's responses (14.1±1.6) was lower than that of ChatGPT-4o (16.4±2.3), Gemini-2.5 (15.8±2.0) and Grok-3 (15.8±1.1) (all P<0.05).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the accuracy, relevance, completeness, and patient comprehensibility of multiple LLMs on early gastric cancer questions, but tests raw model outputs rather than a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
